DILG Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 99 s. 2021 29 July 2021 HON. NANCY A. CATAMCO Govemor Province of Cotabato Dear Govemor Catamco: This has reference to your letter dated 19 July 2021 asking the following queries: I. Whether the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's (SP's) refusal to appropriate funds, when there exists available funds, for programs, projects and activities (PPAs) already incorporated in the Annual Investment Program is reasonable?; 2. Whether those vetoed items which are not overridden by the SP can be reenacted?; 3. If the answer in question no. 2 is in the affirmative, does it mean that the allotments of those deemed reenacted items shall be chargeable against the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the previous year? 4. If the answer in question no. 2 is in the negative, may we know what provision of law that expressly prohibits the reenactment of those vetoed but not overridden items? Per your letter, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) has been refusing or neglecting to appropriate funds for the most vital programs, projects, services and activities (PPAs) within the approved annual investment program despite the availability of funds. On 28 April 2021 , you submitted the first Supplemental Budget of the current year with savings as the main sources of funds along with small amount of reversion. In view of the ongoing health crisis, you certified the proposed supplemental budget as urgent. You also represented that without justifiable reason, the SP arbitrarily slashed the proposed budgetary allocations for priority PPAs for Peace and Order, confidential expenses, donation and other services. Thus, the SP enacted Provincial Ordinance No. 665 approving Supplemental Budget No. I but with a reduced amount, thereby resulting to an unappropriated amount. Pursuant to Section 55 (b) of RA 7160 or the Local Govemment Code of 1991, you vetoed some items in Provincial Ordinance No. 665, including some provisions that do

not relate specifically to a particular appropriation therein for being ultra vires and prejudicial to the public welfare. However, the SP chose not to override the veto. Hence, your above-enumerated queries. In reply to your first question, the reason/s for the alleged "refusal" or "neglect" of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to appropriate funds for the most vital programs, projects, services and activities within the approved annual investment program despite the availability of funds, were not given. Hence, we could not ascertain whether said act or omission is indeed arbitrary as alleged by Governor Catamco. Be that as it may, it may be relevant to emphasize that the Annual Investment Program (AIP) is the yearly program of expenditures both for capital and current requirements of the local government unit (LGU) that serves as the basis for the preparation of Annual and Supplemental Budgetsl. The AIP contains the priority programs, projects, and activities (PPAs) that will directly contribute to the achievement of the goals and objectives of the LGU. As such, the PPAs included in the AIP must be funded under the Annual and Supplemental Budgets. As to the second and third questions, we deem it proper to re-state Section 55 of the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "SECTION 55. Veto Power of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) The local chief executive may veto any ordinance of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, or Sangguniang bayan on the ground that it is ultra vires or prejudicial to the public welfare, stating his reasons therefor in writing. (b) The local chief executive, except the Punong Barangay, shall have the power to veto any particular item or items of an appropriations ordinance, an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program, or an ordinance directing the payment of money or creating liability. In such a case, the veto shall not affect the item or items which are not objected to. The vetoed item or items shall not take effect unless the San unian overrides the veto in the manner herein rovided• otherwise the item or items in the a ro riations ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoedz if any. shall be deemed reenacted. (c) The local chief executive may veto an ordinance or resolution only once. The Sanggunian may override the veto of the local chief executive concerned by two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance effective even without the approval of the local chief executive concerned." (Emphasis Supplied) I DILG Opinion NO. 42, series Of 2015.

The last sentence of Section 55 (b) [the highlighted portion], simply advances the rule that when the local chief executive (LCE) exercises his/her line veto power in an enacted Appropriations Ordinance, those items are simply left for naught. However, the sanggunian concerned may or may not override the said veto, and when they override the same, it is the veto this time which is left dead thereby making the vetoed item deemed approved by the LCE. Definitely, if the Sanggunian concerned succeeds in overriding the LCE's veto, the vetoed items are considered already approved by the LCE. If, however, the veto is not overridden by the sanggunian, the item or items in the Appropriations Ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if any, shall be deemed reenacted.2 In the herein case, the one under consideration is Provincial Ordinance No. 665 approving Supplemental Budget No. 1. A Supplemental Budget is enacted after the Annual Budget has been approved by the local sanggunian. The purpose of a Supplemental Budget is to make changes in the Annual Budget. Instructive on this matter is Section 321 of the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "SECTION 321. Changes in the Annual Budget. - All budgetary proposals shall be included and considered in the budget preparation process. After the local chief executive concerned shall have submitted the executive budget to the Sanggunian, no ordinance providing for a supplemental budget shall be enacted, except when supported by funds actually available as certified by the local treasurer or by new revenue sources. A supplemental budget may also be enacted in times of public calamity by way of budgetary realignment to set aside appropriations for the purchase of supplies and materials or the payment of services which are exceptionally urgent or absolutely indispensable to prevent imminent danger to, or loss of, life or property, in the jurisdiction of the local government unit or in other areas declared by the President in a state of calamity. Such ordinance shall clearly indicate the sources of funds available for appropriations, as certified under oath by the local treasurer and local accountant and attested by the local chief executive, and the various items of appropriations affected and the reasons for the change." Hence, as the local chief executive, when you exercised line veto power on Provincial Ordinance No. 665 and the concerned sanggunian failed to override said veto, those vetoed items are simply left for naught. The items not vetoed remain unaffected. Otherwise stated, the provisions under Provincial Ordinance No. 665 are retained except those vetoed items. Accordingly, reenactment Of the previous year's items corresponding to those vetoed items is proper in this case. This is so because Section 55 of the LGC does not unequivocally restrict veto of appropriations ordinance to that 2 DILG Opinion NO. 45, series Of 2008.

ofthe annual budget only. Section 55 also applies to a supplemental budget The legal maxim that "when the law does not distinguish, neither should we'0 apply in this case. In view of the foregoing discussion, answering the fourth question is no longer necessary. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Unders etary for Local Government LLLS Copy furnished. DIR. JOSEPHINE CABRIDO-LEYSA Regional Director, DILG-Region XII Prime Regional Government Center Carpenter Hill, Koronadal City 3 GR No. 134740, Oct 23, 2001
